hook: The revolutionary who led the Russian Revolution and founded the Soviet Union.

pages.x: Vladimir Ulyanov was born in 1870 in Simbirsk, on the Volga, the son of a school inspector. In 1887 his older brother was hanged for plotting to kill the tsar. That same year Vladimir was thrown out of university for joining a protest.

He became a Marxist revolutionary. In 1897 he was exiled to Siberia for three years, where he married Nadezhda Krupskaya. Later he took the name Lenin, and spent most of the next 17 years abroad, leading the Bolsheviks.
In 1917, after the tsar fell, the German government, at war with Russia, let Lenin cross Germany from Switzerland in a sealed train, hoping he would cause trouble in Russia. He did.
In November 1917 his Bolsheviks seized power in Petrograd and stormed the Winter Palace. Lenin promised "peace, land and bread".

He made peace with Germany, giving up huge lands. A brutal civil war followed. His secret police, the Cheka, jailed and shot many thousands in the Red Terror, and the tsar and his family were killed. Millions died of war and famine.
In 1918 a woman named Fanny Kaplan shot him twice as he left a factory in Moscow. He survived, but never fully recovered.
In 1922 he founded the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, the first communist state, ruled by one party. To rescue the ruined economy, he allowed some private trade again.
Strokes left him unable to speak. In his last notes he warned against Stalin, but the warning was ignored. He died in 1924, and his embalmed body is still on show in a tomb on Red Square.
Lenin led the first communist revolution and founded the Soviet Union, a one-party state that lasted until 1991 and inspired communist movements around the world.
pts: Built a one-party state that ruled by terror
